items.headline: New 3D model reveals how shadows reshape chemistry in stellar nurseries
items.teaser: How do young stars reshape the clouds from which they are born? A new high-resolution 3D model developed by an international team led by …
items.story: How do young stars reshape the clouds from which they are born? A new high-resolution 3D model developed by an international team led by Dr Brandt Gaches from the University of Duisburg-Essen shows how the uneven structure of stellar nurseries creates shadows that alter their chemistry and influence the infrared emission observed by the James Webb Space Telescope. The model has now been published in Astronomy & Astrophysics.

items.story: Quantum computers represent a next step in the fast-paced evolution of technology. Using quantum bits (qubits), they have the potential to run certain calculations exponentially faster than conventional computers. However, developing and fine-tuning quantum computers requires an enormous number of repetitive tests. To accelerate quantum technology development, we need a method that can read quantum states at ultrafast speeds.

items.headline: A highway instead of a racetrack: Strong coupling of light and sound in an optical fiber
items.teaser: For the first time, scientists have achieved strong coupling between light and long-lived acoustic vibrations in an optical fiber. Optica…
items.story: For the first time, scientists have achieved strong coupling between light and long-lived acoustic vibrations in an optical fiber. Optical fibers are used in both classical telecommunications and quantum communication and could serve not only as connections between computing nodes but also as quantum processors themselves in the future. The results, published in Nature Physics, pave the way for new technologies in quantum signal processing.
